name: timos-claude-code-plugins
description: Custom Claude Code plugins for development workflows (generic + per-language + per-topic). See ARCHITECTURE.md for the plugin family conventions.

plugins.name: development-swift
plugins.description: Swift development plugin with code review, formatting/linting, and Swift-specific tooling.

plugins.name: development-go
plugins.description: Go maintenance + review plugin. Review panel: /development-go:review runs 6 specialist agents, with go-resilience-reviewer anchored to the bootstrap sony/gobreaker payload as its reference implementation (#1144). Maintenance dispatches findings from /development:maintenance to go-format-lint-fixer (golangci-lint v2), the static-analysis triage agents go-sonar-triage + go-code-scanning-triage + go-semgrep-triage, go-maintenance-planner, and go-ci-fixer, with a per-package coverage pre-flight (go test -coverprofile) that spawns go-coverage-improver in a worktree when affected code sits below Required. The go-approver synthesis layer posts merge verdicts via /development-go:approve, fed by the 6 review dimensions the Approver walks as risk-register lenses — the panel's own dimension table, resilience included (#1147). The proto-first advisors go-grpc-advisor (buf codegen) and go-api-contract-advisor (grpc-gateway REST facade + 2.0→3.0 OpenAPI pipeline) audit the API-contract wiring. Blessed toolchain: Go modules, Taskfile, golangci-lint v2, go test -coverprofile, buf + grpc-gateway, ko.

plugins.name: development
plugins.description: General development workflow skills for committing, branch naming, and other git operations, plus the shared telemetry/v1 emit + validate contract, its stream-generic rollup, and a committed Grafana reference dashboard for the cross-repo hand-off; ships a PreToolUse(Agent) hook, inert unless switch_fable_to_opus is truthy, that then redirects dispatches whose effective model is fable to opus; bootstrap also ships the blessed Spring, non-Spring-Java, Python and Go resilience + dependency-health payloads (resilience4j for the JVM, circuitbreaker+tenacity for Python, sony/gobreaker for Go, wired to the ops-api /health surface — versioned v1/v2, where v2 serves RFC 9457 problem+json on the two probe 503s while v1 stays frozen, #1330). Gathers kubernetes/IaC findings (Helm/Kustomize/Argo CD manifest presence, Kyverno policy + policy-test detection) for the development-kubernetes topic dispatcher, and OpenTofu/Terraform findings (tofu fmt/validate/tflint/trivy presence detection, plus evaluated state-encryption and pinned-Conftest policy + policy-test checks over *.tf) for the development-opentofu topic dispatcher. Bootstrap also ships the no-cluster-deploy required status check, which fails an application repo whose workflows deploy straight to a cluster (the app-repo half of the image-promotion contract). NOTE for existing repos: a re-run of bootstrap now installs ops-api v2 payloads, whose two probe 503s return RFC 9457 problem+json instead of the v1 {"status":"down"} envelope — see the ops-surface how-to before re-running. ALSO for existing repos: bootstrap's .spectral.yaml is now a thin shim extending one EXACT pinned org styleguide ruleset over jsDelivr (#689) instead of the #692 starter, so a re-run replaces a local ruleset with a remote pin and enforces fifteen org rules at error (four of them a warn->error promotion relative to the #692 starter, nine newly minted) — review the api-styleguide how-to before re-running, and note contracts-lint now needs network access to jsDelivr on every run (no offline fallback, by design), so restricted CI egress or a CDN outage fails the lint until it recovers. resolve-issue detects the repo type at §1b (review-dispatch.zsh detect) and loads the matching development-<repo_type>:resolve-profile when one exists, continuing with its generic rules when none does (#1504). A human's interactive round grant is now persisted mechanically rather than remembered: record-grant.zsh writes the granted ceiling to <work-dir>/.max-rounds and resolve-story-loop.zsh --resume adopts it, reporting the ceiling in force as the new always-present effective_max_rounds / max_rounds_source status keys while max_rounds keeps reporting the value the caller passed (#1576). Residue condition 2 is removed (#1571): the review loop's CONVERGED_WITH_RESIDUE terminal no longer requires every remaining blocker to sit in the previous round's fix-touched set, because scope-findings already confines each round's findings to the story diff — which made the terminal unreachable from the very closing sweep it was built for, since a promoting round runs no fix pass and its set is empty by design. The terminal is correspondingly BROADER: residue now holds on almost any zero-CRITICAL non-convergence, so runs that previously ended in a human escalation may instead open a PR and file the remainder as follow-up issues - and the #1498 possible-false-trip auto-continue is now tried BEFORE residue at that rung, so the loop still spends its free round rather than shipping. resolve-issue's review loop now hands each reviewer a scope block carrying both the repo-relative and absolute spelling of every file plus a verbatim opener naming the worktree to read, and review-dispatch.zsh plan emits worktree_root/original_root/scope_abs — a repo-root file read from the original checkout produced a CRITICAL false positive (#1582). review-dispatch.zsh now applies ONE anchoring rule for --repo: it names the REPOSITORY and every subcommand resolves it to the git toplevel before anything derived is read, so detection, the .maintenance.yml primary and the default findings_path (now absolute, <worktree_root>/.review/findings-round-<N>.json) all describe the same tree, and a subdirectory --repo is a spelling of its repository rather than a scope filter (#1587). bootstrap's IaC path gains the gate MECHANISM (#1603, epic #1602): templates/iac/scripts/k8s-gate.zsh.tmpl, one locally runnable script running render (helm template + kustomize build --enable-helm, so helmCharts: overlays inflate) → schema → lint → policy → config-scan (the pinned trivy binary, embedded checks) → argocd against the rendered tree, one `gate: <stage> ok|skipped — <reason>|FAILED` verdict line per stage, stopping at the first red, every skip reported (an empty repository is green), a missing tool refused before any stage with its brew line, and a developer's working tree left untouched (a symlink-shared policy set is evaluated through a same-depth sibling mirror, never swapped in place). #1604 wires it: kubernetes-ci.yml.tmpl is now ONE job, `gate`, that installs zsh and all seven gate tools at step-level pins (the pins tests/iac-tools.zsh reads for the fixture harness) and runs the repo's gate command, {{GATE_COMMAND}} (render.zsh --gate-command, default make lint, an empty value refused); Makefile.tmpl (lint runs the gate script, hooks sets core.hooksPath) and a two-line hooks/pre-push.tmpl run the same command locally, .maintenance.yml records it as gate: on the kubernetes primary (a KUBERNETES render block), render.zsh carries a template's executable bit to its output, and the gate script and hook are stamped and drift-tracked. #1606 moves IaC-mode branch protection onto it too: branch-protection.sh's IaC mode now requires the single `gate` context instead of the six retired per-stage contexts, and refuses (exit 1, before writing any rule) when .github/workflows/kubernetes-ci.yml cannot report `gate`: it is absent, has no `gate` job, or its `gate` job carries `name:`, a `strategy:` block or a reusable-workflow `uses:` (GitHub would then report the check under another name) - so on an existing IaC repo re-render kubernetes-ci.yml with bootstrap first (that refresh applies to a plugin-rendered file; a hand-written one needs a `gate` job added by hand), then re-run branch protection to drop the six from its rule. #1605 moves bootstrap's §3l flow onto the gate: it emits kubernetes-ci.yml, scripts/k8s-gate.zsh, hooks/pre-push and the Makefile, names the single `gate` context, wires the hook with the new install-iac-hooks.zsh instead of pre-commit (a wiring failure is reported and bootstrap continues), lets a repo with no kubernetes marker bootstrap onto the IaC path on an explicit empty-GitOps-repo confirmation at Q4, and gives preflight.sh an IaC mode that requires gh, jq, git and the gate's seven tools instead of the pre-commit and scanner set. #1583 gives the review loop a carry accounting: reviewers report each carried blocker as confirmed, re-raised (with evidence in the findings file) or unconfirmed, the conductor passes the per-identity records as --carry-accounting (hook mode: the panel's <findings-path>.carry.json sidecar), and the loop refuses a round (CARRY-UNACCOUNTED, exit 2, before verify-<R+1>.json is written) in which a carried blocker was neither confirmed nor re-raised, listing it in the status JSON's always-present carry_unconfirmed and stamping carry_accounting into every accepted round's changelist. #1584 makes a read-only reviewer's tool-verdict claim a SUGGESTION until the conductor runs the tool: resolve-issue §3.5's round protocol gains a *decided pass* that, after the gate has been observed green — or, on a round the boundary runs with no gate, after the panel — and before consolidation, runs every read-only `decides:` command a finding names — as written, never substituted — against the round's minted tree in the worktree root, records exit + first output lines to `<work-dir>/decided-<R>.log`, and rewrites the severity to the reviewer's `proposed-severity` only on a real red (a green and a command that could not run each leave it a logged SUGGESTION; a malformed finding is recorded and promotes nothing, its severity changed in neither direction). The pass settles a finding on the round that RAISES it; re-deciding a promotion the loop then carries is a stated KNOWN LIMITATION filed as #1647, and the reviewer half ships with every panel's read-only reviewers, repo-wide (#1644). consolidate-findings.zsh accepts an optional per-finding `decided` ("red"|"green") and carries it onto every changelist item, blocking and suggestions alike, as a visible RECORD — never a mechanism, so it sets no severity, priority or blocking; on dedup only group members sharing the representative title contribute (an empty title is not a match key), a red anywhere in the group additionally exempts the item from the `--adjudicated` drop, and a finding without the field is byte-identical to before. Since #1485 resolve-story-loop.zsh refuses a FULL round whose scope is empty — no story diff, or only loop-owned files changed — as STALE_FINDINGS (the EMPTY-STORY-DIFF arm), whether its panel wrote no findings file or an actual [], instead of converging on a review that saw nothing. register-claude-apps.zsh keeps ONE registry entry PER OWNER (#1682): --org <slug> registers an organisation's App pair beside the personal one (organisation-owner rights checked before the browser opens), --apps <list> registers a subset (--apps claude-maintenance is writer-only), apps.json becomes schema 2 keyed by owner with Keychain services claude-plugins.<owner>.<app>, and a schema-1 apps.json is migrated in place on first use (backup at apps.json.v1.bak); owner keys are lower-cased. Every consumer now picks the App pair by the OWNER OF THE CURRENT REPOSITORY (#1683): the mint scripts, install-claude-apps.zsh (including --writer-only), bootstrap's --claude-approver auto-detection and its Step 4.5 preflight share one helper, claude-apps-owner.zsh (status reports each App as registered, not registered or key missing for that owner), so an organisation repo mints the organisation's App and a personal repo the personal one with no flag; a missing owner or App fails with the exact register-claude-apps.zsh [--org <slug>] --apps <app> command and never falls through to another owner, and a schema-1 apps.json is refused naming register-claude-apps.zsh --list. The #1682 compatibility aliases are gone: the next register-claude-apps.zsh run deletes the legacy Keychain items first and only then drops the top-level keys and alias_owner from apps.json, retrying on the next run when a delete fails. /development:resolve-issue now emits its own telemetry/v1 record (#1226): a single-issue run that reaches the dependency precheck appends exactly one pipeline:"resolve-issue" record at whichever ending it reaches (success on a PR, parked at the readiness gate or the precheck, escalated, failed; a Step 0 stop appends none), through story-telemetry.zsh and the pure payload builder build-story-telemetry-record.zsh, and it is never fatal. The skill takes --telemetry-file PATH / --telemetry-dir DIR in any position and forwards them, with a pre-minted --parent-run-id, to every resolve-story-loop.zsh invocation, which gains both flags, a <work-dir>/.telemetry-run-ids ledger and an in-repo --telemetry-dir loop-internal exclusion; ARCHITECTURE.md records the per-pipeline instrumentation conventions every later pipeline follows. Bootstrap now composes its quality workflows, setup guide and pre-commit config per resolved tool instead of from two whole visibility trees (#1670): toolchain-templates.zsh selects the tool-scoped templates and render.zsh's per-tool block tags compose the jobs, so every toolchain resolve-tools.zsh accepts is composed; resolve-tools.zsh now also rejects CodeQL on a private repository (it needs GitHub Advanced Security). Branch protection, the setup preflight and State D's gap-fill now take that resolved toolchain instead of visibility (#1671): branch-protection.sh and preflight.sh take --static-analysis / --vulnerabilities and no longer accept a visibility flag, the required contexts follow the #1670 D1 rule (analyze (<lang>) only when codeql.yml is on disk), preflight checks each resolved tool's prerequisites, Step 4.5's setup automation runs one script per tool under that tool's own trigger (setup-sonarcloud.sh, setup-sonarqube.sh, register-runner.sh, setup-snyk.sh, enable-github-security.sh) and never re-applies branch protection, which Step 4b applies once (#1769), and bootstrap no longer stops at its plan for a non-default toolchain. resolve-issue runs a story size pre-flight before its first edit (#1437): the session declares the files it intends to touch, size-preflight.zsh stops a plan over its file-count threshold, one that straddles plugins or one that edits bootstrap templates together with any other owned file outside the bootstrap skill, and a stop is overridden by the human or parked with the needs-split label; every verdict is a story-preflight telemetry record.

plugins.name: development-python
plugins.description: Python maintenance dispatcher — fixes ruff / semgrep / Code Scanning / SonarCloud findings autonomously via per-tool agents in parallel worktrees, auto-bumps deps (patch + minor + major) with test-based verification. Favors autonomy over speed: expect tens-of-thousands of tokens per run.

plugins.name: development-java
plugins.description: Java/Gradle maintenance plugin — full-maintenance tier mirroring development-python. Dispatches per-tool agents (Spotless, SonarCloud, CodeQL/Scorecard, semgrep, Dependabot/Snyk PRs, Gradle major upgrades) in worktrees, with a JaCoCo coverage pre-flight; ships the java-approver reviewer + /development-java:approve. JDK runtime upgrades land in a later slice (#308).

plugins.name: development-spring
plugins.description: Spring framework TOPIC plugin — composes alongside development-java for Java + Spring Boot 4+ repos (baseline Spring Framework 7 / Jakarta EE 11; older Boot lines out of scope). Audits Spring configuration via spring-config-advisor, plus a conforms-to-ops-api check whose recommendations branch on whether the repo has adopted the Spring resilience payload (which owns /health via its opshealth endpoint); reuses java-ci-fixer for CI. Incremental: config audit in v0.1; a Spring Boot version-upgrade agent, bootBuildImage, and the contract-first API drift gate land in later slices (#296). Since #1330 the ops-api check also requires the two probe 503s to be served as bare RFC 9457 problem+json documents (ops-api v2) — including on the bespoke non-payload route, which a green ops-conformance run does not verify.

plugins.name: development-claude-plugin
plugins.description: Plugin family for projects that ARE Claude Code plugins. Ships a test harness (/development-claude-plugin:test), a review panel (/development-claude-plugin:review — prose logic, contract integrity, script quality, tests, manifests), and a maintenance dispatcher that validates plugin conventions and composes alongside the language plugin. Validators: version sync, SKILL.md/agent frontmatter, orphaned skill/agent references, directory layout, and shell-script quality (shellcheck / zsh -n). Its five read-only reviewers (contract-integrity, prose-logic, script-reviewer, test-reviewer, manifest-check) now carry a byte-identical evidence rule (#1584): a finding whose claim IS a tool run's verdict — a linter would flag this, a suite run would come back red, a validator would reject this, a version-sync script would report a mismatch — is capped at SUGGESTION unless the reviewer ran the tool and quotes it, and instead names `decides: <read-only command>` plus the `proposed-severity:` the conductor may promote it to on a real red, with a slot for both lines in each Reporting Format. The line it draws is observation vs. execution, not subject matter, so a defect read straight out of the artifacts — two manifests disagreeing about a version, a changed script with no test file beside it — keeps full severity under the agent's own bar.

plugins.name: development-docs
plugins.description: Language-agnostic documentation topic plugin. Composes ALONGSIDE the language plugin via /development:maintenance (a TOPIC plugin, like development-spring), triggered by the docs/architecture/ marker. Ships the c4_drift finding source (declared C4 containers vs detected reality → docs-c4-drift-advisor).

plugins.name: development-javascript
plugins.description: JavaScript/TypeScript maintenance plugin (foundation slice, #729). Receives findings from /development:maintenance, validates its JSON payload, and dispatches the format_lint group to js-format-lint-fixer (ESLint --fix + Prettier --write), with js-ci-fixer handling CI-failure remediation on the resulting PRs. Blessed toolchain installed by /development:bootstrap: flat eslint.config.js, Prettier @120, vitest + v8 coverage, a strict tsconfig base, npm, and Node 24 LTS. The contract-consumer machinery (orval typed client + MSW), the review panel, static-analysis triage, coverage, vendor PRs, and the approver land in later slices of #683.

plugins.name: development-react
plugins.description: React framework topic plugin (foundation slice, #956). Composes ALONGSIDE development-javascript via /development:maintenance (a TOPIC plugin, like development-spring composes with development-java), triggered by the React marker — `react` in the runtime dependencies of any package.json — and only when javascript is also detected. This slice ships the composition wiring only: a real but tool-less gather that places `react` in supported_topics, and a dispatcher stub returning a zero-group plan, reusing js-ci-fixer for CI remediation.

plugins.name: development-kubernetes
plugins.description: Infrastructure-as-code topic plugin for Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, Kustomize overlays and Argo CD resources. Composes ALONGSIDE a language plugin, and can itself be PRIMARY for a repo with no application language (a GitOps repo). Charter — mechanism only: render and validate manifests, and run the repo's own Kyverno policies from policies/kyverno/**/*.{yaml,yml}, skipping when no policy file matches. Defers Dockerfiles and image builds to language plugins (language-first). Ships no approver agent — a cluster definition is approved by a human. This slice adds the five agents and the review panel (#1153): the security, reliability and Argo CD review dimensions behind /development-kubernetes:review, plus the manifest fixer and policy triage agents the maintenance dispatcher now routes every finding group to. Its CI pipeline ships as a `development` bootstrap template — six requirable checks over rendered manifests (#1154).

plugins.name: development-opentofu
plugins.description: Infrastructure-as-code topic plugin for cloud provisioning — OpenTofu and Terraform-compatible HCL: .tf/.tf.json sources, module structure, provider and version constraints, backend and state configuration, and .tfvars hygiene. Composes ALONGSIDE a language plugin, and can itself be PRIMARY for a repo with no application language (a provisioning repo). Charter — mechanism only: run the static checks, plus the consumer's own Conftest policies from policies/conftest/**/*.rego (the policy step alone skips when no file matches; the static checks always run). One opinion is held as a first-class check rather than left to a consumer policy: state must be encrypted at rest — checked dialect-aware, not one dialect's block, and binding only where the repo owns state. Defers what the modules deploy INTO a cluster to development-kubernetes, and images and application code to the language plugins (language-first); the boundary is the file set, so cluster resources expressed in HCL stay here. Ships no approver agent — a provisioning change can destroy state no rollback recovers, so a human approves. Named for the MPL-2.0 tool; BUSL-licensed Terraform is supported, not endorsed. This slice adds the maintenance dispatch: the ownership boundary and the marketplace registration (#1159), plus the gather script, topic marker and dispatcher (#1160). Until the agents land the dispatcher routes nothing — it escalates every group for human action, naming the agent the group will route to. The four agents and the review panel (#1161), the bootstrap check pipeline (#1162), and the self-contained test fixtures (#1163) follow.

plugins.name: development-composition
plugins.description: Composition topic plugin — the per-constellation deployment repo type. A composition repo depends on no repository: it pins its members' published container images in a `.claude-workspace.yaml` constellation manifest, declares the environments they are promoted through, and owns promotion. This plugin owns that manifest's `claude-workspace/v1` contract and the validator that enforces it; it does NOT own the member repos' code, contracts or images, which stay with their language plugins. Like development-kubernetes and development-opentofu it can be PRIMARY, because a composition repo has no application language of its own — but not yet: the marker, gather and dispatch land with #1747, so a `primary: composition` declaration today is stale and selects nothing. This slice (#1744) lands the boundary, the contract and `validate-workspace.zsh` — nothing calls the validator yet: the bootstrap scaffold and promote-to-prod workflow are #1745, the Renovate image-tag config #1746, the topic marker, gather script and maintenance dispatch #1747, the injection-hardened bump-triage agent #1748 and the how-to #1749. Deployment itself stays out: `deploy_target` accepts only `none` until the compose (#719) and Kubernetes (#720) renderers land, and no run ever reports a deploy that did not happen.
